claimsAndLimits: D1 pricing meters scanned row work, including index work; returned rows are a different quantity.
D1 documents a 100000-byte statement limit and 32 arguments per SQL function; the native local runtime accepted a larger JSON call, so the new query is constrained to the documented contract.
Separate CLI statements do not establish one held snapshot; read-replication/sequential-consistency documentation is not a transaction-freeze guarantee.
Fetch Metadata describes request mode/context and is emitted for potentially trustworthy URLs in conforming implementations. It does not authenticate a person or the UA-declared engine.
The Fetch Standard explicitly supports WebDriver BiDi emulated User-Agent values; a parsed Firefox-family claim is not an authenticated Firefox process.

The checked Fetch Metadata Working Draft section 4.2 calls these forbidden response-header names. The normative Fetch Standard instead places the sec- prefix under forbidden request-header rules, separately from Set-Cookie/Set-Cookie2 response headers. That terminology discrepancy is not copied into implementation claims.
